institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That i felt it was a destination that offered a welcoming vibe towards exchange students, meaning that it was quite sure that you found some good communities to engage in

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. The home institution made sure that we knew what to prepere and NTNU also provided some extra information when we arrived.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the first week we had "lectures" about the things we were responsible for getting in order ourselfs. And also different organisations told os about different opportunities to join different trips and communities. We had information meetings and get sent checklists - these were very helpfull

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was okay easy. I found housing at
Hybel.no
where i found a room in a "kollektiv" that i shared with three norwegian girls. I really recommend this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you find a private room somewhere, it is good opportunity to get to know some locals and to get naturally closer to the culture of your destination

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You are responsible for signing up for classes and exams yourself. Therefore you have to check that exam dates don't overlap. This was a little difficult as the dates were visible quite late. Other than that it was okay easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could find good help at NTNU's website

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes that I wished for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at NTNU's webpage for help if you need it. It will probably be there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was okay, maybe a little easier than what I usually experience in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At NTNU, I didnt have classes where we had "øvelsestimer" which I've had in most of my courses at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
FARM3003: Pharmaceutical Innovation
INTRO175: Introduction to Norway
MOL3014: Nanomedicine 1
MOL3023: Molecular Bacteriology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I was very happy for the INTRO175 course as it was a nice way to get a broad understanding of Norway. It also had some good teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Norway has a lot of beautiful sites that it really cool to experience. But taking trips can also be a little expensive. My advice is to try and plan some of them yourself (except if it's through NTNUI), as you often can do it cheaper that when signing up with an organisation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I had heard a lot about that food should be really expensive, but I actually didn't think it was a lot different from in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There's NTNUI who provides a group/community for pretty much every kind of sport/activity

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the "NTNUI Topptur og Frikjøring group" who had training sessions every monday - this was really fun (and hard). I also joined the "NTNUI Surf Group" for a surftrip to Hoddevik in November, I can really recommend this!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go see all of Norways beautiful nature!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy, I don't think it is much more different from in Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I actually can't come up with anything..

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The many and easy opportunities for getting outdoor experiences!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: start as soon as possible to look for housing and get your exchange documents in order, it is nice to have this in order!
2: join every opportunity you get to go on trips and experiences, it is probably more cool than you would have thought
3: don't feel stressed or get fomo, you will reach everything

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Join NTNUI!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experiences I had with the other exchange students

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To focus on school when there were so many nice people and things to do

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
